## Facebook

**Platform:** Facebook  
**Caption:**

Most cars in Hawthorn and Kew look fine — until you point a detail light at the bonnet.

Automated car washes are the most common cause of paint damage we see. The spinning brushes carry grit from the car before yours, dragging it across your clear coat thousands of times a session. Over two, three, four years, the damage accumulates: a full-panel haze of swirl marks that's invisible in a car park but unmistakable in direct sun.

This week we brought a 2022 BMW 540i back from four years of that exact treatment. Two-stage paint correction removed the swirl marks completely. Ceramic coating sealed the corrected finish so it doesn't happen again.

The owner estimated it'd been through an auto wash at least 150 times. That's 150 sessions of slow, compounding damage we reversed in a single day — at his home in Kew, no workshop drop-off required.

If your car's been on the same routine, tag a mate who needs to hear this, or book a paint inspection via the link below.

## LinkedIn

**Platform:** LinkedIn  
**Caption:**

Most professionals driving a $90K car have no idea what four years of auto washes have done to their paint.

The damage isn't dramatic. It accumulates slowly: swirl marks from brushes carrying grit across the clear coat, compounding session by session. Under normal lighting it's invisible. Under a detail light — or in direct sun at the right angle — it reads as a full-panel haze that no amount of washing removes. It's not dirt. It's structural damage to the clear coat itself.

We detailed a 2022 BMW 540i this week. The owner described it as "fine" — maintained, regularly washed, no visible scratches. Under our detail light, the bonnet and doors were covered wall to wall in swirl marks from four years of automated wash use. The correction took two stages and a full day. The result was better than factory finish. Ceramic coating was applied on top, backed by a manufacturer warranty, so it holds.

The business case for getting this right isn't cosmetic. A paint-corrected and ceramic-coated vehicle holds its resale value better than one with degraded clear coat — and at trade-in, the difference in perceived condition can move the needle by thousands. Paint correction before sale or lease return is one of the highest-ROI preparation steps available. We've seen it repeatedly across BMWs, Mercs, and Audis across Melbourne's Inner East.

If you drive a vehicle worth protecting, or manage a fleet where resale and condition matter, a paint inspection costs nothing. We come to your office car park. DM us or comment below.
